Level after the EQ (-24 to +24 dB).
Auto Gain: offsets the average level change of the bell and shelf bands, so a brighter or fuller setting is not judged as better just for being louder.
Zero Latency runs the bands as minimum-phase filters; Linear Phase gives the same magnitude with no phase shift (5120 samples of latency, reported for delay compensation).
uses: Everyday corrective and tonal EQ on any track, with up to eight bands
Steep low and high cuts (up to 96 dB/oct) to clean up rumble and hiss
Mid/side EQ on the mix bus: mono the lows, open up the side highs
Linear-phase mastering EQ that keeps transients and stereo image intact
Fix a single side of a stereo recording with Left or Right bands
studio_eq.properties: Eight bands in series, each a bell, shelf (RBJ), notch, band pass, or a low or high cut built as a Butterworth cascade of 1 to 16 poles (6 to 96 dB/oct; Q 0.71 is flat, higher Q lifts the corner). Each band runs on stereo, mid, side, left or right. Zero Latency: biquad cascades, no latency. Linear Phase: the same magnitude response as a 2x2 matrix per frequency bin (so mid/side and left/right bands combine exactly), turned into four 8192-tap FIRs (Hann window) and run by 16384-point FFT convolution in 1024-sample blocks; latency 5120 samples, reported for delay compensation. Auto Gain: minus the mean level change of the bell and shelf bands over 64 log-spaced points from 20 Hz to 20 kHz (mid and stereo bands count fully, left and right half, side not), within ±24 dB. The GFX and VST3/CLAP interfaces draw the response over a live spectrum (post, pre or off); drag a node to set its frequency and gain.

spectral_ducker.card_desc: Make Room for a Vocal, Band by Band
spectral_ducker.keywords: spectral ducker sidechain ducking trackspacer vocal space carve mix masking frequency ducking dynamic eq kick bass voice over 32 band
slider_desc: How deep the track can be cut in each band (0 to 100% = up to 24 dB).
Key level per band above which the track ducks (-60 to 0 dB); the dashed line in the display.
How fast the cut follows the key (0.1 to 100 ms).
How fast the track comes back when the key stops (10 to 1000 ms).
Bands below this frequency never duck (20 Hz to 5 kHz).
Bands above this frequency never duck (200 Hz to 20 kHz).
What ducks: both channels (Stereo), only the Mid, or only the Side, which keeps the centre intact and makes room at the edges.
Blend of ducked and dry track (0 to 100%).
Level after the ducker (-12 to +12 dB).
Output plays the ducked track; Delta plays only what is taken out, to hear exactly where the ducker works.
uses: Carve space for a lead vocal in a busy instrumental or pad bus
Let the kick through the bass only where they overlap
Voice-over over music that stays full between the words
Duck a reverb or delay return by the dry signal it comes from
Side-only ducking to clear the edges for a centred vocal
spectral_ducker.properties: The key (track channels 3/4, summed to mono) runs through 32 fourth-order band passes, a third of an octave apart from 30 Hz to 18 kHz; each band's level follows with Attack and Release. Every 16 samples, where a band is above Threshold, its excess (up to Amount × 24 dB) sets the cut of a Q 3 bell on the same band of the track; the bells overlap, so each cuts 0.43 of its band's amount and together they cut about the amount. Bells at 0 dB pass the signal unchanged. Stereo, mid or side; Mix and Output; Listen Delta plays dry minus ducked. Zero latency. In the Rack, the key is the Rack's dry input.

reference.card_desc: A/B Your Mix Against a Reference
reference.keywords: reference track a/b compare comparison level match loudness matched lufs short-term mix mastering correlation spectrum mono check side
slider_desc: What you hear: the Track (your mix, channels 1/2) or the Reference (channels 3/4); the switch crossfades over 10 ms.
Level Match: plays the reference at your mix's short-term loudness, so the comparison is about tone and balance, not volume.
Extra gain on the reference (-12 to +12 dB), on top of the match.
Monitor: Stereo, Mono (both channels summed) or Side (the difference only), for both sources.
uses: A/B a mix against a commercial track at the same loudness
Check a master's tonal balance and width against a reference
Compare two versions of a mix routed to the same track
Mono and side checks of mix and reference with one switch
reference.properties: Both inputs are K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770) and measured as short-term loudness (the last 3 s, every 100 ms). With Level Match on, the reference's gain moves a tenth of the way to the difference every 100 ms (about a second to settle), within ±24 dB, and holds while either source is below -60 LUFS; Trim is added. Listen crossfades linearly over 10 ms. Monitor folds after the switch. The interfaces show both loudnesses, the reference's gain, each source's stereo correlation (averaged over about 3 s) and both spectra (each bin averaged over about a second, the reference at its played gain). No latency, no Rack module (it needs a second stereo input).
